cues.en: There is a hole at the bottom of math. A hole that means we will never know everything with certainty. There will always be true statements that cannot be proven. Now, no one knows what those statements are exactly, but they could be something like the twin prime conjecture. Twin primes are prime numbers that are separated by just one number, like 11 and 13, or 17 and 19.
cues.zh: 在数学的根基处存在着一个漏洞。一个意味着我们永远无法确定一切的漏洞。总会有一些为真却无法被证明的陈述。目前没人确切知道这些陈述到底是什么，但它们可能就像孪生素数猜想一样。孪生素数是指彼此只差 2 的两个素数，比如 11 和 13，或者 17 和 19。

cues.en: And as you go up the number line, primes occur less frequently, and twin primes are rarer still. But the twin prime conjecture is that there are infinitely many twin primes you never run out. As of right now, no one has proven this conjecture true or false. But the crazy thing is this. We may never know. Because
cues.zh: 随着数轴向后延伸，素数出现的频率越来越低，孪生素数更是少之又少。但孪生素数猜想认为，孪生素数有无穷多个，永远不会用尽。截至目前，还没人能证明这个猜想是对是错。但最离谱的事情在于：我们可能永远都不会知道答案。因为……

cues.en: What has been proven is that in any system of mathematics where you can do basic arithmetic, there will always be true statements that are impossible to prove. That is life. Specifically, this is the game of life created in 1970 by mathematician John Conway. Sadly, he passed away in 2020 from COVID-19.
cues.zh: 已经得到证明的是：在任何能进行基本算术的数学系统中，总会存在不可能被证明的真命题。这就是人生。具体来说，这是数学家 John Conway 在 1970 年发明的康威生命游戏（Game of Life）。遗憾的是，他已于 2020 年因 COVID-19 去世。

cues.en: Conway's Game of Life is played on an infinite grid of square cells, each of which is either live or dead, and there are only two rules. One, any dead cell with exactly three neighbors comes to life, and two, any living cell with less than two or more than three neighbors dies. Once you've set up the initial arrangement of cells, the two rules are applied to create the next generation.
cues.zh: 康威生命游戏是在一个无限的方格网格上进行的，每个方格要么是活的，要么是死的，而且规则只有两条。第一，任何恰好有三个活邻居的死细胞都会复活；第二，任何活邻居少于两个或多于三个的活细胞都会死亡。一旦设定好了细胞的初始排列，这两条规则就会应用于生成下一代。

cues.en: and then the one after that, and the one after that, and so on. It's totally automatic. Conway called it a zero-player game. But even though the rules are simple, the game itself can generate a wide variety of behavior. Some patterns are stable once they arise, they never change. Others oscillate back and forth in a loop. A few can travel across the grid forever, like this glider here. Many patterns just fizzle out. But a few...
cues.zh: 接着是下下一代，再下一代，如此循环往复。它完全是自动运行的。康威称它为零玩家游戏。不过尽管规则很简单，游戏本身却能产生极其丰富的行为。有些图案一旦出现就很稳定，永远不会改变。有些则在循环中来回震荡。少数图案可以永远在网格上移动，就像这里的滑翔机一样。许多图案最终就慢慢消失了。但还有少数……

cues.en: keep growing forever. They keep generating new cells. Now you would think that given the simple rules of the game, you could just look at any pattern and determine what will happen to it. Will it eventually reach a steady state? Or will it keep growing without limit? But it turns out this question is impossible to answer. The ultimate fate of a pattern in Conway's Game of Life is undecidable, meaning
cues.zh: 永远增长下去。它们会不断生成新的细胞。你可能会觉得，鉴于游戏规则如此简单，随便看一个图案就能断定它会变成什么样。它是最终达到稳定状态呢？还是会无限增长下去？但事实证明，这个问题是无法回答的。康威生命游戏中图案的最终宿命是不可判定的，这意味着

cues.en: There is no possible algorithm that is guaranteed to answer the question in a finite amount of time. You could always just try running the pattern and see what happens, I mean the rules of the game are a kind of algorithm after all, but that's not guaranteed to give you an answer either, because even if you run it for a million generations, you won't be able to say whether it'll last forever or just two million generations, or a billion, or a Googleplex.
cues.zh: 不存在任何可行的算法，能保证在有限时间内给出答案。你当然可以直接运行这个图案看看会发生什么，毕竟游戏规则本身也是一种算法，但这同样无法保证给你一个确切的答案，因为即便你运行了一百万代，你也无法断定它会永远延续下去，还是只能维持两百万代、十亿代，亦或是古戈尔普勒克斯代。

cues.en: Is there something special about the game of life that makes it undecidable? Nope. There are actually a huge number of systems that are undecidable. Wang tiles, quantum physics, airline ticketing systems, and even Magic the Gathering. To understand how undecidability shows up in all of these places, we have to go back 150 years to a full-blown revolt in mathematics.
cues.zh: 是生命游戏有什么特别之处，才导致它不可判定吗？并不是。实际上，有非常多的系统都是不可判定的。王氏砖、量子物理、机票预订系统，甚至是《万智牌》（Magic the Gathering）。要理解不可判定性是如何出现在所有这些领域的，我们必须回到 150 年前数学界的一场全面变革。

cues.en: In 1874 Georg Cantor, a German mathematician, published a paper that launched a new branch of mathematics called set theory. A set is just a well-defined collection of things. So the two shoes on your feet are a set, as are all the planetariums in the world. There's a set with nothing in it, the empty set, and a set with everything in it.
cues.zh: 1874 年，德国数学家 Georg Cantor 发表了一篇论文，开创了数学的一个新分支——集合论。集合就是某些明确对象的汇集。比如你脚上穿的两只鞋是一个集合，世界上所有的天文馆也是一个集合。有一个什么都不包含的集合叫做空集，也有一个包含一切的全集。

cues.en: Now Cantor was thinking about sets of numbers, like natural numbers, positive integers like 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on, and real numbers, which include fractions like a third, five halves, and also irrational numbers like pi, e, and the square root of 2. Basically, any number that can be represented as an infinite decimal. He wondered, are there more natural numbers? Or more real numbers between 0 and 1?
cues.zh: 当时康托尔正在思考数集的问题，比如像 1、2、3、4 这样的正整数，即自然数，以及实数，实数包括像三分之一、二分之五这样的分数，还有像圆周率、自然常数 e 和根号 2 这样的无理数，基本上就是任何可以表示为无限小数的数字。他想知道，是自然数更多，还是 0 到 1 之间的实数更多？

cues.en: The answer might seem obvious. There are an infinite number of each, so both sets should be the same size. But to check this logic, Cantor imagined writing down an infinite list, matching up each natural number on one side with a real number between 0 and 1 on the other.
cues.zh: 答案看似显而易见：两者都有无穷多个，所以这两个集合的大小应该是一样的。但为了验证这个逻辑，康托尔设想列出一个无限列表，把一侧的每个自然数，与另一侧 0 到 1 之间的某个实数一一对应起来。

cues.en: Now since each real number is an infinite decimal, there is no first one so we can just write them down in any random order. The key is to make sure we get them all with no duplicates and line them up one-to-one with an integer. If we can do that with none left over, well then we know that the set of natural numbers and the set of real numbers between 0 and 1 are the same size.
cues.zh: 由于每个实数都是无限小数，并没有所谓的“第一个”，所以我们可以按任意顺序写下来。关键是要确保把它们全部列出、不重不漏，并与整数一一对应。如果我们能做到这一点且一个不剩，那就能证明自然数集和 0 到 1 之间的实数集大小是相同的。

cues.en: So, assume we've done that. We have a complete infinite list with each integer acting like an index number, a unique identifier for each real number on the list. Now, Cantor says, start writing down a new real number. And the way we're gonna do it is by taking the first digit of the first number and adding one. Then take the second digit of the second number and again add one.
cues.zh: 好，假设我们已经做到了这一点。我们有了一个完整的无限列表，每个整数都像一个索引号，也就是列表中每个实数的唯一标识符。现在，Cantor说，开始写下一个新的实数。我们的做法是：取第一个数字的第一位小数，然后加一；接着取第二个数字的第二位小数，同样加一。

cues.en: Take the third digit of the third number, add 1, and keep doing this all the way down the list. If the digit is a 9, just roll it back to an 8. And by the end of this process, you'll have a real number between 0 and 1. But here's the thing. This number won't appear anywhere on our list. It's different from the first number in the first decimal place, different from the second number in the second decimal place, and so on down the line.
cues.zh: 再取第三个数字的第三位小数，加1，以此类推沿着列表一直做下去。如果某一位是9，就把它变回8。在这个过程结束时，你就会得到一个介于0和1之间的实数。但关键在于，这个数字不会出现在我们列表中的任何地方。它的小数点后第一位与第一个数不同，小数点后第二位与第二个数不同，依此类推。

cues.en: It has to be different from every number on the list by at least one digit, the number on the diagonal. That's why this is called Cantor's diagonalization proof. It shows there must be more real numbers between 0 and 1 than there are natural numbers extending out to infinity. So not all infinities are the same size. Cantor called these countable and uncountable infinities respectively.
cues.zh: 它至少有一位数字与列表中的每一个数都不同，也就是对角线上的那个数字。这就是为什么这被称为康托尔对角线证明。它表明，0 到 1 之间的实数数量，必然多于一直延伸到无穷大的自然数数量。因此，并不是所有的无穷大都一样大。康托尔分别将它们称为可数无穷和不可数无穷。

cues.en: And in fact, there are many more uncountable infinities which are even larger. Now Cantor's work was just the latest blow to mathematics. For 2,000 years, Euclid's elements were considered the bedrock of the discipline. But at the turn of the 19th century, Loboszewski and Gauss discovered non-Euclidean geometries. And this prompted mathematicians to examine more closely the foundations of their field. And they did not like what they saw.
cues.zh: 事实上，还有许多甚至更大的不可数无穷。康托尔的研究只是对数学界的最新一记重击。两千年来，欧几里得的《几何原本》一直被视为该学科的基石。但在 19 世纪之交，Lobachevsky 和 Gauss 发现了非欧几里得几何。这促使数学家们更加仔细地审视他们领域的根基。而眼前的景象让他们大失所望。

cues.en: The idea of a limit, at the heart of calculus, turned out to be poorly defined. And now Cantor was showing that infinity itself was much more complex than anyone had imagined. In all this upheaval, mathematics fractured and a huge debate broke out among mathematicians at the end of the 1800s. On the one side were the intuitionists who thought that Cantor's work was nonsense. They were convinced that math was a pure creation of the human mind and that infinities like Cantor's
cues.zh: 微积分核心的极限概念，被发现定义得很不严谨。而当时 Cantor 又证明了无穷本身远比任何人想象的要复杂得多。在这一片动荡中，数学界发生了分裂，并在19世纪末的数学家之间爆发了一场大争论。一方是直觉主义者，他们认为 Cantor 的研究纯属无稽之谈。他们坚信数学纯粹是人类大脑的创造，而像 Cantor 提出的那种无穷

cues.en: weren't real. Henri Poincaré said that later generations will regard set theory as a disease from which one has recovered. Leopold Kronecker called Cantor a scientific charlatan and a corruptor of the youth, and he worked to keep Cantor from getting a job he wanted. On the other side were the formalists. They thought that math could be put on absolutely secure logical foundations through Cantor's set theory.
cues.zh: 根本就不存在。Henri Poincaré 曾说，后人会把集合论看作一种已经痊愈的疾病。Leopold Kronecker 则骂 Cantor 是学术骗子、荼毒青年，还百般阻挠 Cantor 获得他想要的工作。而另一方则是形式主义者。他们认为，借助 Cantor 的集合论，可以为数学奠定绝对可靠的逻辑基础。

cues.en: The informal leader of the formalists was the German mathematician David Hilbert. Hilbert was a living legend, a hugely influential mathematician who had worked in nearly every area of mathematics. He almost beat Einstein to the punch on general relativity. He developed entirely new mathematical concepts that were crucial for quantum mechanics, and he knew that Cantor's work was brilliant.
cues.zh: 形式主义学派事实上的领袖是德国数学家 David Hilbert。Hilbert 是一位活着的传奇，是一位极具影响力的数学家，其研究几乎涵盖了数学的每一个领域。他甚至差点在广义相对论上抢在 Einstein 之前发表。他提出了对量子力学至关重要的全新数学概念，而且他深知 Cantor 的工作有多么出色。

cues.en: Hilbert was convinced that a more formal and rigorous system of mathematical proof based on set theory could solve all the issues that had cropped up in math over the last century, and most other mathematicians agreed with him. No one shall expel us from the paradise that Cantor has created, Hilbert declared. But in 1901, Bertrand Russell pointed out a serious problem in Cantor's set theory. Russell knew that if sets can contain anything, they can contain other sets, or even themselves.
cues.zh: Hilbert 坚信，基于集合论建立一个更加形式化、更加严格的数学证明体系，就能解决上个世纪数学界出现的全部问题，大多数数学家也对此表示赞同。Hilbert 宣称：“没有人能把我们从 Cantor 开辟的乐园中驱逐出去。”但在 1901 年，Bertrand Russell 指出了 Cantor 集合论中的一个严重漏洞。Russell 意识到，如果集合可以包含任何东西，那么它们就可以包含其他集合，甚至包含它们自己。

cues.en: For example, the set of all sets must contain itself, as does the set of sets with more than five elements in them. You could even talk about the set of all sets that contain themselves. But this leads straight to a problem. What about R, the set of all sets that don't contain themselves? If R doesn't contain itself, well, then it must contain itself. But if R does contain itself, then by definition, it must not contain itself. So
cues.zh: 比如，所有集合的集合必然包含它自身，元素数量超过五个的集合构成的集合也是如此。你甚至可以讨论包含自身的所有集合所构成的集合。但这直接引出了一个问题。如果是 R，即所有不包含自身的集合所构成的集合呢？如果 R 不包含自身，那么它就必须包含自身。但如果 R 确实包含自身，根据定义，它就一定不能包含自身。所以

cues.en: R contains itself if and only if it doesn't. Russell had found another paradox of self-reference, and he later explained his paradox using a hairy analogy. Let's say there's a village populated entirely by grown men with a strange law against beards. Specifically, the law states that the village barber must shave all and only those men of the village who do not shave themselves.
cues.zh: R 包含自身，当且仅当它不包含自身。Russell 发现了又一个自指悖论，后来他用一个胡子拉碴的比喻解释了这个悖论。假设有一个全都是成年男子的村庄，那里有一条针对胡子的奇怪法律。具体来说，法律规定，村里的理发师必须给村里所有不给自己刮胡子的人刮胡子，而且只给这些人刮。

cues.en: But the barber himself lives in the village too, of course, and he's a man, so who shaves him? If he doesn't shave himself, then the barber has to shave him. But the barber can't shave himself, because the barber doesn't shave anyone who shaves themselves, so the barber must shave himself if and only if he doesn't shave himself. It's a contradiction. The intuitionists rejoiced at Russell's paradox, thinking it had proven set theory hopelessly flawed.
cues.zh: 当然，理发师自己也住在这个村里，他也是个男人，那谁来给他刮胡子呢？如果他不给自己刮，那就得由理发师来给他刮。但理发师又不能给自己刮，因为理发师从不给那些自己刮胡子的人刮，所以理发师当且仅当不给自己刮胡子时，才能给自己刮胡子。这就产生了矛盾。直觉主义者对罗素悖论拍手称快，认为这证明了集合论有着无可救药的缺陷。

cues.en: But Zermelo and other mathematicians from Hilbert School solved the problem by restricting the concept of a set. So the collection of all sets, for example, is not a set anymore. And neither is the collection of all sets which don't contain themselves. This eliminated the paradoxes that come with self-reference. Hilbert and the formalists lived to fight another day, but self-reference refused to die quite that easily.
cues.zh: 但策梅洛和希尔伯特学派的其他数学家通过限制集合的概念解决了这个问题。比如，所有集合的汇集，就不再是一个集合了。所有不包含自身的集合的汇集，也不是集合了。这就消除了由自指带来的悖论。希尔伯特和形式主义者暂时渡过了难关，但自指可没那么容易被彻底消灭。

cues.en: Fast forward to the 1960s and mathematician Hao Wang was looking at square tiles with different colors on each side like these. The rules were that touching edges must be the same color and you can't rotate or reflect tiles, only slide them around. The question was, if you're given an arbitrary set of these tiles, can you tell if they will tile the plane? That is, will they connect up with no gaps all the way out to infinity? It turns out...
cues.zh: 快进到1960年代，数学家王浩当时正在研究每条边颜色各异的方形地砖，就像这些一样。规则是相接的边缘必须颜色相同，而且地砖不能旋转或翻转，只能平移。问题在于，如果给你任意一组这样的地砖，你能判断出它们能否铺满整个平面吗？也就是说，它们能否毫无缝隙地一直拼接延伸到无穷远？结果表明……

cues.en: You can't tell for an arbitrary set of tiles whether they will tile the plane or not. The problem is undecidable. Just like the fate of a pattern in Conway's Game of Life. In fact, it's exactly the same problem. And that problem, ultimately, comes from self-reference, as Hilbert and the formalists were about to discover.
cues.zh: 对于任意一组地砖，你无法判断它们到底能否铺满整个平面。这个问题是不可判定的。就像 Conway 的《生命游戏》中某个图案的最终命运一样。事实上，它们本质上是完全相同的问题。而这个问题归根结底源自自指，正如 Hilbert 和形式主义者们即将发现的那样。

cues.en: Hilbert wanted to secure the foundations of mathematics by developing a new system for mathematical proofs. Systems of proof were an old idea going back to the ancient Greeks. A system of proofs starts with axioms, basic statements that are assumed to be true, like a straight line can be drawn between any two points. Proofs are then constructed from those axioms using rules of inference, methods for using existing statements to derive new statements, and these are chosen to preserve truth.
cues.zh: 希尔伯特希望通过构建一套新的数学证明系统，来稳固数学的根基。证明系统是一个古老的概念，最早可以追溯到古希腊时期。证明系统始于公理，也就是被假定为真的基础陈述，比如任意两点之间都可以画一条直线。随后，人们利用推理规则从这些公理出发构建证明，这些规则是利用现有陈述推导出新陈述的方法，其选择标准是要保证真值不变。

cues.en: If the existing statements are true, then so are the new ones. Hilbert wanted a formal system of proof, a symbolic logical language with a rigid set of manipulation rules for those symbols. Logical and mathematical statements could then be translated into this system. If you drop a book, then it will fall would be A then B. And no human is immortal would be expressed like this.
cues.zh: 如果现有的陈述为真，那么新推导出的陈述也必定为真。希尔伯特希望建立一个形式化的证明系统，即一种符号逻辑语言，并为这些符号配有一套严格的推演规则。逻辑和数学陈述随后都可以被翻译进这个系统。比如，“如果你扔下一本书，它就会掉落”可以表示为“若 A 则 B”。而“没有人是长生不老的”则可以这样表示。

cues.en: Hilbert and the formalists wanted to express the axioms of mathematics as symbolic statements in a formal system, and set up the rules of inference as the system's rules for symbol manipulation. So Russell, along with Alfred North Whitehead, developed a formal system like this in their three-volume Principia Mathematica, published in 1913. Principia Mathematica is vast, a total of nearly 2,000 pages of dense mathematical notation.
cues.zh: 希尔伯特和形式主义学派希望将数学公理表示为形式系统中的符号陈述，并将推理规则设定为该系统操作符号的规则。于是罗素与阿尔弗雷德·诺思·怀特海合作，在他们于1913年出版的三卷本《数学原理》中构建了这样一个形式系统。《数学原理》篇幅浩繁，整整近两千页全是密密麻麻的数学符号。

cues.en: It takes 762 pages just to get to a complete proof that 1 plus 1 equals 2, at which point Russell and Whitehead dryly note, the above proposition is occasionally useful. The authors had originally planned a fourth volume, but unsurprisingly, they were too worn out to complete it.
cues.zh: 光是彻底证明 1 加 1 等于 2 就花了整整 762 页，罗素和怀特海还在那儿冷幽默地加了一句：“上述命题偶尔还是挺有用的。”作者们原本还计划写第四卷，但毫不意外，他们已经心力交瘁，实在写不动了。

cues.en: So yes, the notation is dense and exhausting, but it is also exact, unlike ordinary languages. It leaves no room for errors or fuzzy logic to creep in. And most importantly, it allows you to prove properties of the formal system itself. There were three big questions that Hilbert wanted answered about mathematics. Number one, is math complete? Meaning, is there a way to prove
cues.zh: 所以没错，这种记号密集又让人头大，但它也很精确，不像日常语言那样模糊。它杜绝了任何错误或模糊逻辑乘虚而入的可能。最重要的是，它能让你证明形式系统本身的各种性质。关于数学，希尔伯特当时希望能解答三个大问题。第一，数学是完备的吗？也就是说，是否有一种方法可以证明

cues.en: every true statement. Does every true statement have a proof? Number two, is mathematics consistent? Meaning, is it free of contradictions? I mean, if you can simultaneously prove A and not A, then that's a real problem because you can prove anything at all. And number three, is math decidable? Meaning, is there an algorithm that can always determine whether a statement follows from the axioms?
cues.zh: 每一个真命题？每个真命题都能得到证明吗？第二，数学是一致的吗？也就是说，它里面没有任何矛盾吗？我的意思是，如果你能同时证明 A 和非 A，那可就出大问题了，因为这样你就能证明任何事情。第三，数学是可判定的吗？也就是说，是否存在一个算法，总能判定某个命题是否能由公理推导出来？

cues.en: Now, Hilbert was convinced that the answers to all three of these questions was yes. At a major conference in 1930, Hilbert gave a fiery speech about these questions. He ended it with a line that summed up his formalist dream. These words are literally on his grave.
cues.zh: 当时，Hilbert坚信这三个问题的答案都是肯定的。在1930年的一次重要学术会议上，Hilbert针对这些问题发表了一场充满激情的演讲。他在结尾用一句话总结了自己的形式主义之梦。这句话如今就刻在他的墓碑上。

cues.en: By the time Hilbert gave this speech, his dream was already crumbling. Just the day before, at a small meeting at the same conference, a 24-year-old logician named Kurt Gödel explained that he had found the answer to the first of Hilbert's three big questions about completeness. And the answer was no. A complete, formal system of mathematics was impossible.
cues.zh: 就在Hilbert发表演讲时，他的梦想其实已经在破灭了。就在前一天同一场会议的小组讨论上，一位名叫Kurt Gödel的24岁逻辑学家表示，他已经找到了Hilbert关于完备性这第一个大问题的答案。而答案是否定的。一个完备的数学形式系统是不可能存在的。

cues.en: The only person who paid much attention was John von Neumann, one of Hilbert's former students, who pulled Gödel aside to ask a few questions. But the next year, Gödel published a proof of his incompleteness theorem, and this time everyone, including Hilbert, took notice. This is how Gödel's proof works. Gödel wanted to use logic and mathematics to answer questions about the very system of
cues.zh: 当时唯一真正关注的人是Hilbert以前的学生John von Neumann，他拉住Gödel问了几个问题。但到了第二年，Gödel发表了他那不完备性定理的证明，这一次包括Hilbert在内的所有人都注意到了。Gödel的证明是这样展开的。Gödel想用逻辑和数学本身，来回答关于这一系统本身的问题。

cues.en: logic and mathematics. And so he took all these basic symbols of a mathematical system, and then he gave each one a number. This is known as the symbol's Gödel number. So the symbol for not gets the number 1, or has the Gödel number 2, if then is Gödel number 3. Now if you're expressing all of these symbols with numbers, then what do you do about the numbers themselves?
cues.zh: 于是他把数学系统中所有的基础符号都拿出来，给每一个都赋予了一个数字。这就是所谓的符号的Gödel数。比如“非”符号对应数字1，“或”对应的Gödel数是2，“如果……那么……”是Gödel数3。既然你用数字来表示所有这些符号，那数字本身该怎么办呢？

cues.en: Well, 0 gets its own goodle number, 6. And if you want to write a 1, you just put this successor symbol next to it. The immediate successor of 0 is 1. And if you want to write 2, then you have to write SS0. And that represents 2, and so on. So you could represent any positive integer this way. Granted, it is cumbersome, but it works. And that is the point of this system. So now that we have...
cues.zh: 好，0 有它自己的哥德尔数，也就是 6。如果你想写 1，只要在它旁边加上这个后继符号就行。0 的紧邻后继就是 1。如果你想写 2，就得写成 SS0。这就代表了 2，以此类推。所以你可以用这种方式表示任何正整数。诚然，这很繁琐，但确实管用。而这正是这个系统的意义所在。那么现在我们已经给……

cues.en: good old numbers for all of the basic symbols and all of the numbers we might wanna use, we can start to write equations. Like we could write zero equals zero. So these symbols have the good old numbers six, five, six. And we can actually create a new card that represents this equation, zero equals zero. And the way we do it is we take the prime numbers,
cues.zh: 所有基本符号以及我们可能用到的所有数字都分配好了哥德尔数，我们就可以开始写方程了。比如我们可以写 0 等于 0。这些符号的哥德尔数分别是 6、5、6。我们实际上可以制作一张新卡片来代表这个方程，也就是 0 等于 0。具体做法是，我们取一系列质数，

cues.en: starting at 2, and we raise each one to the power of the goodle number of the symbol in our equation. So we have 2 to the power of 6 times 3 to the power of 5 times 5 to the power of 6 equals 243 million. So 243 million is the goodle number of the whole equation 0 equals 0. We can write down goodle numbers for any set of symbols that you can imagine.
cues.zh: 从 2 开始，把每个质数分别以方程中对应符号的哥德尔数作为指数进行幂运算。所以我们得到 2 的 6 次方乘以 3 的 5 次方乘以 5 的 6 次方，等于 2 亿 4300 万。因此 2 亿 4300 万就是“0 等于 0”这整个方程的哥德尔数。我们能为你想象到的任何符号集合写出对应的哥德尔数。

cues.en: So really this is an infinite deck of cards where any set of symbols that you want to write down in a sequence you can represent with a unique goodle number. And the beauty of this goodle number is you can do a prime factorization of it and you can work out exactly what symbols made up this card. So in this whole pack of cards there are going to be true statements and there are going to be false statements.
cues.zh: 所以这其实是一副无限大的卡牌，你想按顺序写下的任何符号组合，都可以用一个唯一的哥德尔数来表示。而这个哥德尔数的妙处在于，你可以对其进行质因数分解，从而准确推导是哪些符号构成了这张卡牌。所以在这整副卡牌中，既会有真命题，也会有假命题。

cues.en: So how do you prove that something is true? Well, you need to go to the axioms. The axioms also have their own good old numbers which are formed in the same way. So here's an axiom which says not the successor of any number x equals zero. Which makes sense because in this system there are no negative numbers and so the successor of any number cannot be zero. So we can put down this axiom
cues.zh: 那么你要如何证明某个命题为真呢？其实，你需要回溯到公理。公理同样拥有自己的哥德尔数，也是以相同方式生成的。比如这里有一条公理，它表示任何数 x 的后继都不等于 0。这很合理，因为在这个系统中没有负数，所以任何数的后继都不可能是 0。于是我们就可以列出这条公理

cues.en: And then we can substitute in 0 for x saying that 1 does not equal 0. And we've created a proof, this is the simplest proof I can think of that shows that 1 does not equal 0. Now this card for the proof of 1 does not equal 0 gets its own goodle number. And the way we calculate this goodle number is just as before we take the prime numbers and we raise 2 to the power of
cues.zh: 然后我们可以把 x 替换为 0，从而得出 1 不等于 0。这样我们就完成了一个证明，这也是我能想到的证明 1 不等于 0 的最简证明。现在，这张代表“1 不等于 0”的证明卡牌也有了属于它自己的哥德尔数。计算这个哥德尔数的方法和之前一样，我们取质数，然后计算 2 的

cues.en: the axiom times 3 to the power of 1 does not equal 0. And we get a tremendously large number. It would have 73 million digits if you calculated it all out. So I've just left it here in exponential notation. As you can see...
cues.zh: 公理次方，乘以 3 的“1 不等于 0”次方。我们会得到一个极其巨大的数字。如果把它全部算出来，它将拥有 7300 万位数字。所以我在这里直接保留了它的指数表示形式。正如你所看到的……

cues.en: these numbers get very large and so you might want to start just calling them by letters. So we could say this one is good old number A, this is good old number B, good old number C, and so on. Good old goes to all this trouble to find this card, which says there is no proof for the statement with good old number G. The trick is that the good old number of this card is G.
cues.zh: 这些数字变得非常大，所以你可能想直接用字母来称呼它们。我们可以说这张是哥德尔数 A，这张是哥德尔数 B，哥德尔数 C，等等。哥德尔费尽周折找到了这样一张卡片，上面写着：哥德尔数为 G 的命题是不可证明的。而玄机在于，这张卡片本身的哥德尔数恰好就是 G。

cues.en: So what this statement is really saying is this card is unprovable. There is no proof anywhere in our infinite deck for this card. Now think about it. If it's false and there is a proof, then what you have just proven is there is no proof. So you're stuck with a contradiction. That would mean the mathematical system is inconsistent. The other alternative
cues.zh: 所以这个命题真正表达的是：这张卡片是不可证明的。在我们这副无限的卡牌中，根本找不到这张卡片的证明。现在仔细想想：如果它是假的，并且存在一个证明，那么你刚才证明出的却是“不存在证明”。你就陷入了矛盾。这意味着数学系统是不一致的。而另一种可能，

cues.en: that this card is true. There is no proof of the statement with good old number G, but that means this mathematical system has true statements in it that have no proof. So your mathematical system is incomplete and that is Goodall's incompleteness theorem. This is how he shows that any basic mathematical system that can do fundamental arithmetic will always have statements within it which are true
cues.zh: 就是这张卡片是真的。哥德尔数为 G 的命题确实没有证明，但这意味着该数学系统中存在无法被证明的真命题。所以你的数学系统是不完备的，这就是哥德尔不完备定理。他就是这样证明了：任何能够进行基础算术的基本数学系统，其中必定始终存在某些命题，它们是真命题，

cues.en: but which have no proof. There's a line in the TV show The Office that echoes the self-referential paradox of Goodall's proof.
cues.zh: 但却无法被证明。电视剧《The Office》里有一句台词，正好呼应了哥德尔证明中的这种自指悖论。

cues.en: are not at all the same thing. Hilbert was wrong. There will always be true statements about mathematics that just cannot be proven. Now Hilbert could console himself with the hope that at least we could still prove math's consistent, that is free of contradictions, but then Gödel published his second incompleteness theorem in which he showed that any consistent formal system of math cannot prove its own consistency. So
cues.zh: 根本就不是同一回事。希尔伯特错了。数学中总会有一些真正成立的陈述，是根本无法被证明的。当时希尔伯特还可以聊以自慰，心想至少我们还能证明数学是一致的，也就是没有矛盾；但接着哥德尔发表了他的第二不完备定理，指出任何一致的数学形式系统，都无法证明自身的一致性。所以

cues.en: Taken together, Goodall's two incompleteness theorems say that the best you can hope for is a consistent yet incomplete system of math, but a system like that cannot prove its own consistency. So some contradiction could always crop up in the future, revealing that the system you'd been working with had been inconsistent the whole time.
cues.zh: 综合来看，哥德尔的两大不完备定理表明，你最多只能指望得到一个一致但并不完备的数学系统，可这样的系统却无法证明自身的一致性。因此，未来随时都可能冒出某种矛盾，揭示出你一直以来所使用的系统自始至终都是不一致的。

cues.en: And that leaves only the third and final big question from Hilbert, is mathematics decidable? That is, is there an algorithm that can always determine whether a statement follows from the axioms? And in 1936, Alan Turing found a way to settle this question. But to do it, he had to invent the modern computer. In his time, computers weren't machines, they were people, often women who carried out long and tedious calculations.
cues.zh: 这就只剩下希尔伯特提出的第三个、也是最后一个大问题：数学是可判定的吗？也就是说，是否存在某种算法，总能判定一个命题是否可以从公理推导出来？1936年，Alan Turing 找到了解决这个问题的办法。但为了做到这一点，他不得不发明现代计算机。在他那个时代，“计算机”指的不是机器，而是人，通常是承担冗长乏味计算工作的女性。

cues.en: Turing imagined an entirely mechanical computer. He wanted it to be powerful enough to perform any computation imaginable, but simple enough that you could reason through its operation. So he came up with a machine that takes as input an infinitely long tape of square cells, each containing a zero or a one. The machine has a read-write head that can read one digit at a time, and then it can perform one of only a few tasks.
cues.zh: Turing 构想出一种完全机械化的计算机。他希望它足够强大，能执行任何想象得到的计算，同时又足够简单，让人能推导明白它的运行过程。于是，他设计出这样一台机器：它输入一条由方格组成的无限长纸带，每个格子里写着 0 或 1。机器配有一个读写头，每次可以读取一个数字，然后只能执行极少数几种操作中的一种。

cues.en: Overwrite a new value, move left, move right, or simply halt. Halting means the program has run to completion. Now the program consists of a set of internal instructions. You can think of it like a flowchart that tells the machine what to do based on the digit it reads and its internal state. You could imagine exporting these instructions to any other Turing machine, which would then perform in exactly the same way as the first.
cues.zh: 覆写一个新值、向左移动、向右移动，或者直接停机。停机意味着程序已经运行完毕。这里的程序由一组内部指令组成。你可以把它想象成一个流程图，根据读取的数字和自身的内部状态，来告诉机器下一步该做什么。你可以想象把这些指令导出到任何其他图灵机上，它的运行方式就会和第一台完全一模一样。

cues.en: Although this sounds simple, a Turing machine's arbitrarily large memory and program mean it can execute any computable algorithm if given enough time, from addition and subtraction to the entire YouTube algorithm. It can do anything a modern computer can. That's what made the Turing machine so useful in answering Hilbert's question on decidability. When a Turing machine halts, the program has finished running and the tape is the output.
cues.zh: 虽然这听起来很简单，但图灵机任意大的内存和程序意味着，只要给它足够的时间，它就能执行任何可计算的算法，从小到加减法，大到整个 YouTube 的推荐算法。现代计算机能做的一切，它都能做。这也正是图灵机在解答希尔伯特的可判定性问题时如此有用的原因。当图灵机停机时，程序运行结束，纸带上的内容就是最终的输出。

cues.en: But sometimes a Turing machine never halts. Maybe it gets stuck in an infinite loop. Is it possible to tell beforehand if a program will halt or not on a particular input? Turing realized this halting problem was very similar to the decidability problem. If he could find a way to figure out if a Turing machine would halt, then it would also be possible to decide if a statement followed from the axioms.
cues.zh: 但有时图灵机永远不会停机。它可能会陷入死循环。那有没有可能事先判断出一个程序在特定输入下是否会停机呢？图灵意识到，这个停机问题和可判定性问题非常相似。如果他能找到判断图灵机是否会停机的方法，那也就能判定一个命题是否能由公理推导出来。

cues.en: For example, you could solve the twin prime conjecture by writing a Turing machine program that starts with the axioms and constructs all theorems that can be produced in one step using the rules of inference. Then, it constructs all theorems that can be produced in one step from those, and so on. Each time it generates a new theorem, it checks if it's the twin prime conjecture. And if it is, it halts. If not, it never halts.
cues.zh: 举个例子，你可以通过编写一个图灵机程序来解决孪生素数猜想：从公理出发，利用推理规则构造出所有能一步推导出的定理。接着，再从这些定理出发构造出下一步能推导出的所有定理，以此类推。每次生成一个新定理，它就会检查这是否是孪生素数猜想。如果是，它就停机；如果不是，它就永不停机。

cues.en: So if you could solve the halting problem, you could solve the twin prime conjecture and all sorts of other unsolved questions. So Turing said, let's assume we can make a machine H that can determine whether any Turing machine will halt or not on a particular input. You insert the program and its input, and H simulates what will happen, printing out either halts or never halts.
cues.zh: 所以如果你能解决停机问题，就能解决孪生素数猜想以及各种其他未解难题。图灵说，假设我们能造出一台机器 H，它可以判断任意图灵机在特定输入下是否会停机。你输入程序和对应的输入数据，H 就会模拟运行结果，输出“停机”或“永不停机”。

cues.en: For now, we don't worry about how H works. We just know that it always works. It always gives you the right answer. Now, we can modify the H machine by adding additional components. One, if it receives the output halts, immediately goes into an infinite loop. Another, if it receives never halts, then it immediately halts. We can call this entire new machine H+, and we can export the program
cues.zh: 目前我们先不管 H 是怎么运作的。我们只知道它总是管用，总是能给出正确答案。现在，我们可以给机器 H 加上额外的组件来进行改造。其中一个组件，在收到“停机”输出时，会立刻陷入死循环。另一个组件，在收到“永不停机”时，则会立刻停机。我们可以把这整台新机器叫做 H+，并且把整台机器的程序

cues.en: for that entire machine. Now what happens if we give this machine its own code both as program and input? Well now H is simulating what H plus would do given its own input. Essentially H has to determine the behavior of a machine that it itself is a part of in this exact circumstance. If H concludes that H plus
cues.zh: 导出出来。现在如果我们把这台机器自身的代码，同时作为程序和输入喂给它，会发生什么呢？这时 H 正在模拟 H+ 接收自身输入时的行为。本质上，H 必须在这种特定情境下，判断一台包含它自身的机器的行为。如果 H 得出的结论是 H+

cues.en: never halts. Well, this makes H plus immediately halt. If H thinks H plus will halt, then that necessarily forces H plus to loop. Whatever output the halting machine H gives, it turns out to be wrong. There's a contradiction. The only explanation can be that a machine like H can't exist. There's no way to tell in general if a Turing machine will halt or not on a given input.
cues.zh: 永不停机，那么这会让 H+ 立刻停机。如果 H 认为 H+ 会停机，这又必然会迫使 H+ 陷入死循环。无论停机机器 H 给出什么输出，结果都是错的。这就产生了矛盾。唯一的解释只能是，像 H 这样的机器根本不可能存在。普遍来说，根本没办法判断一台图灵机在给定输入下到底会不会停机。

cues.en: And this means mathematics is undecidable. There is no algorithm that can always determine whether a statement is derivable from the axioms. So something like the twin prime conjecture might be unsolvable. We might never know whether there are infinite twin primes or not. The problem of undecidability even crops up in physical systems.
cues.zh: 这意味着数学是不可判定的。没有任何算法能始终判定一个命题能否从公理中推导出来。所以像孪生素数猜想这样的问题可能根本无解。我们可能永远都无法知道孪生素数是不是无限的。不可判定性甚至还会出现在物理系统中。

cues.en: In quantum mechanics, one of the most important properties of a many-body system is the difference in energy between its ground state and its first excited state. This is known as the spectral gap. Some systems have a significant spectral gap, whereas others are gapless. There are a continuum of energy levels all the way down to the ground state. And this is important because at low temperatures, gapless quantum systems can undergo phase transitions, while gapped systems cannot.
cues.zh: 在量子力学中，多体系统最重要的性质之一就是基态与第一激发态之间的能量差。这就是所谓的能隙。有些系统具有明显的能隙，而另一些系统则是无能隙的。在一直延伸到基态的范围内存在连续的能级。这很重要，因为在低温下，无能隙量子系统会发生相变，而有能隙系统则不会。

cues.en: They don't have the energy needed to overcome the spectral gap. But figuring out if a system is gapped or gapless has long been known to be a very difficult problem. Only recently, in 2015, did mathematicians prove that in general the spectral gap question is undecidable. To quote the authors,
cues.zh: 它们没有足够的能量来跨越能隙。但长期以来，判断一个系统是否有能隙一直是个公认的难题。直到最近的2015年，数学家们才证明了一般情况下谱隙问题是不可判定的。引用作者的原话，

cues.en: to deduce its macroscopic properties. Now remember that Turing designed his machines to be as powerful computers as it is possible to make. To this day, the best computational systems are those that can do everything a Turing machine can. This is called Turing completeness, and it turns out there are many such Turing-complete systems. Although they are powerful, every Turing-complete system comes with a catch.
cues.zh: 来推导其宏观性质。现在别忘了，图灵设计他的机器是为了打造尽可能强大的计算机。时至今日，最优秀的计算系统仍然是那些能做到图灵机所能做的一切的系统。这被称为图灵完备性，事实证明存在许多这样的图灵完备系统。尽管它们功能强大，但每个图灵完备系统都有一个隐患。

cues.en: its own analog of the halting problem, some undecidable property of the system. Wang tiles are Turing-complete, their halting problem is whether or not they'll tile the plane. Complex quantum systems are Turing-complete, and their halting problem is the spectral gap question. And the game of life is Turing-complete, its halting problem is literally whether or not it halts.
cues.zh: 它们各自对应停机问题的版本，也就是系统的某种不可判定属性。王氏砖是图灵完备的，它们的停机问题就是能否铺满平面。复杂的量子系统也是图灵完备的，它们的停机问题则是谱隙问题。而康威生命游戏同样是图灵完备的，它的停机问题照字面看，就是它究竟会不会停下来。

cues.en: There are many more examples of this, like airline ticketing systems, Magic the Gathering, PowerPoint slides, and Excel spreadsheets. Nearly every programming language in existence is designed to be Turing-complete. But in theory, we only need one programming language because, well, you can program anything at all using any Turing-complete system. So here's a Turing machine inside the game of life. And since the game of life is itself Turing-complete,
cues.zh: 类似的例子还有很多，比如航司票务系统、《万智牌》、PowerPoint 幻灯片以及 Excel 表格。现存的几乎所有编程语言都被设计成了图灵完备的。但在理论上，我们其实只需要一种编程语言，因为只要是图灵完备的系统，你就能用它编出任何东西。所以瞧，这就是生命游戏里的图灵机。而且既然生命游戏本身也是图灵完备的，

cues.en: It should be capable of simulating itself, and indeed, it is. This is the game of life. Running on the game of life. The real legacy of David Hilbert's dream is all of our modern computational devices. Kurt Gödel suffered bouts of mental instability later in life. Convinced that people were trying to poison him, he refused to eat, eventually starving himself to death.
cues.zh: 它理应能够模拟自身，事实上它确实可以。这就是生命游戏，运行在生命游戏之上。David Hilbert 梦想留下的真正遗产，是我们所有的现代计算设备。Kurt Gödel 晚年深受精神不稳定发作的折磨。他深信有人想毒害自己，因而拒绝进食，最终活活把自己饿死了。

cues.en: Hilbert died in 1943. His epitaph was his slogan from 1930. We must know, we will know. The truth is, we don't know. Sometimes, we can't know. But in trying to find out, we can discover new things, things that change the world.
cues.zh: 希尔伯特逝世于 1943 年。他的墓志铭就是他 1930 年的名言：我们必须知道，我们必将知道。但事实是，我们并不知道。有时候，我们根本不可能知道。但正是在探寻未知的过程中，我们才能发现新事物，发现那些改变世界的事物。

cues.en: Alan Turing put his ideas about computing to practical use in World War II, leading the team at Bletchley Park that built real calculating machines to crack Nazi codes for the Allies. By one estimate, the intelligence Turing and his colleagues gathered from decrypted messages shortened the war by two to four years. After the war, Turing and John von Neumann designed the first true programmable electronic computer, ENIAC, based on Turing's designs. But...
cues.zh: 二战期间，Alan Turing 将他对计算的构想付诸实践，带领布莱切利园的团队制造出真正的计算机，为盟军破译纳粹密码。据估算，Turing 和他的同事从破译情报中收集到的信息，让战争缩短了两到四年。战后，Turing 和 John von Neumann 根据 Turing 的设计，打造了第一台真正可编程的电子计算机 ENIAC。然而……

cues.en: Turing didn't live to see his ideas develop much further. In 1952, the British government convicted him of gross indecency upon learning he was gay. He was stripped of his security clearance and forced to take hormones. In 1954, he committed suicide. Turing changed the world. He is widely considered to be the most important founding figure in computer science. All modern computers are descended from his designs. But Turing's ideas about computability
cues.zh: Turing 没能活着看到自己的思想进一步发扬光大。1952 年，英国政府在发现他是同性恋后，判处他“严重猥亵罪”。他被剥夺了安全许可，并被迫接受激素治疗。1954 年，他自杀身亡。Turing 改变了世界。他被广泛公认为计算机科学最重要的奠基人。所有现代计算机都源自他的设计。但 Turing 关于可计算性的思想，

cues.en: came from his concept of the Turing machine, which came from thinking about Hilbert's question, is math decidable? So Turing's code-breaking machines and indeed all modern computers stem from the weird paradoxes that arise from self-reference. There is a hole at the bottom of math, a hole that means we will never know everything with certainty. There will always be true statements that cannot be proven.
cues.zh: 其实源自他的图灵机概念，而这又源于对希尔伯特问题的思考：数学是可判定的吗？因此，Turing 的破译机，乃至所有现代计算机，都源于自我引用带来的诡异悖论。数学的底层存在一个漏洞，这个漏洞意味着我们永远无法确定地知晓一切。永远都会存在无法被证明的真命题。

cues.en: And you might think this realization would have driven mathematicians mad and led to the disintegration of the entire mathematical enterprise. But instead, thinking about this problem transformed the concept of infinity, changed the course of a world war, and led directly to the invention of the device you're watching this on right now.
